summary: Calculates per-pixel neighbor differences across horizontal, vertical, or depth/array directions to create slope data.
common_gotchas: Default normalized output can hide signed negative slopes unless you use float output and zeropoint 0.
Z slope sources only make sense for 3D textures or 2D texture arrays.
Neutral output means zeropoint, not always a hardcoded 0.5.
Edge results depend on the Extend menu.
key_concepts: Slope TOP computes differences between neighboring pixels and writes selected horizontal, vertical, or Z slope data into output channels.
A neutral value is based on zeropoint, with 0.5 as the default display-friendly midpoint.
32-bit float output plus zeropoint 0 is better for signed slope data.
The operator supports 3D textures and 2D texture arrays, where Z options sample depth/slice direction.
